children: The EBITDA margin improved to 18.2 per cent from 13.5 per cent in the year-ago quarter, an expansion of 473 basis points

Ramkrishna Forgings reported a 54.9 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) increase in consolidated revenue from operations to Rs 1,405.42 crore in the second quarter of financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27), supported by healthy domestic demand and resilient export market activity.

The company's profit after tax (PAT) stood at Rs 70.59 crore in Q2FY27, compared with a loss of Rs 9.50 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. PAT had stood at Rs 47 crore in the preceding quarter.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) more than doubled to Rs 256.23 crore in Q2FY27, compared with Rs 122.54 crore a year earlier, registering a growth of 109.1 per cent.
The EBITDA margin improved to 18.2 per cent from 13.5 per cent in the year-ago quarter, an expansion of 473 basis points.
For the first half of FY27, the company's consolidated revenue increased 36.4 per cent to Rs 2,622.09 crore, compared with Rs 1,922.79 crore in H1FY26.
EBITDA for the first half rose 75.1 per cent to Rs 474.70 crore, while the EBITDA margin improved to 18.1 per cent from 14.1 per cent in the corresponding period last year.
PAT for H1FY27 stood at Rs 117.47 crore, compared with Rs 2.29 crore in the year-ago period.

Commenting on the results, Naresh Jalan, Managing Director of Ramkrishna Forgings, said domestic demand remained healthy, supported by firm commercial vehicle production schedules, while customer activity across key export markets remained resilient.

The company is also expanding its manufacturing capabilities. Its forged wheels facility near Chennai, established through a joint venture with Titagarh Rail Systems, is nearing commercial production. The project is expected to expand its presence in the Indian Railways supply chain.
The company is also ramping up its casting operations and adding capacities and value-added products to serve customers across passenger vehicles, electric vehicles and industrial applications.
During the quarter, the promoters completed the conversion of warrants, infusing Rs 150 crore into the company to support its balance sheet and ongoing business requirements.

Looking ahead, Ramkrishna Forgings is seeking to expand its presence in non-ferrous forgings, including aluminium, titanium, Inconel and Nimonic grades. These materials are intended for high-technology applications across aerospace, robotics and semiconductors.
Jalan said the company's focus would remain on improving capacity utilisation, disciplined execution and strengthening its balance sheet as it pursues long-term growth opportunities.
